title: Coverage Increases Requested by the Insured — Billing Rule, NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
## Coverage increases the insured requests without a loan transaction

A pending coverage increase that the insured requested with no loan transaction, put into effect on a NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own) policy on a tier that carries no ICC coverage, is billed on the terms below.

**Scope of the measure.** For a pending coverage increase the insured requested with no loan transaction on a tier that carries no ICC coverage, and only for such a request, the increase on the risk premium line is measured as the rise rule of this schedule states; a pending coverage increase recorded for a loan transaction follows the rise rule written for such requests, and every other coverage increase or deductible decrease keeps the base measure: the risk premium component is the increase in the full-term risk premium and the ICC premium component is the increase in the full-term ICC premium.

**Scope of the dating.** For a pending coverage increase the insured requested with no loan transaction on a tier that carries no ICC coverage, and only for such a request, the increase takes effect on the date the dating and limit rules of this schedule give; a pending coverage increase recorded for a loan transaction follows the dating rules written for such requests, and new business and every other mid-term coverage increase or deductible decrease take effect at 12:01 a.m. on the day that is the tier's standard waiting period in calendar days after the date the signed application (or endorsement request) and the full premium are received.

A request on a tier that carries ICC coverage is not handled by this schedule: it is referred to the underwriting desk and nothing is charged under this schedule.

**Business effect of billing.** The increase takes effect on the latest of the dates the dating and limit rules give, the policy takes the limits and deductibles recorded on the request, and the rated risk premium on the policy is raised by the rise in the full-term risk premium on which the charge is measured. Endorsement charges are posted to the premium account for the current term on the risk premium line and the reserve fund assessment line, each referencing the request; a charge of zero is not posted.

### Calling `bill_insured_increase_9da169e7`

`bill_insured_increase_9da169e7` is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it. It puts the pending request into effect with the figures supplied; it checks no eligibility and computes nothing.

- `dwelling_policy_id` — the reference number of the NFIP Dwelling Form policy being endorsed, as returned by the policy lookup.
- `dwelling_change_id` — the reference number of the pending coverage-increase request, as returned by the servicing-document lookup for that policy.
- `change_effective_date` — the date the coverage increase takes effect, written YYYY-MM-DD (calendar date, no time zone).
- `risk_premium_charge` — the endorsement charge on the risk premium line, in US dollars as a non-negative number with 2 decimal places, already rounded half-up to the cent.
- `reserve_fund_charge` — the endorsement charge on the reserve fund assessment line, in US dollars as a non-negative number with 2 decimal places, already rounded half-up to the cent.
- `endorsed_risk_premium` — the full-term risk premium that stands on the policy once the increase is in effect, in US dollars with 2 decimal places.

On success the request record is stamped with `change_effective_date`, the policy takes the limits and deductibles recorded on the request and `endorsed_risk_premium`, and each non-zero charge is posted and raises the amount owed. The receipt reads: "Coverage increase <request reference> effective <YYYY-MM-DD> on policy <policy reference>; contents <limit>; charges posted: <entry reference> <component> <amount>, ...; balance now <amount>." — limits in whole US dollars, amounts in US dollars with 2 decimals, the balance being the amount owed.
